assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is the disclosure/ToS gate over an emit-action at a downstream handoff; this is not legal advice
disclosure is mandatory and must travel in-band so the downstream session cannot strip it
the downstream handoff is a single point of failure that defaults to block on any unmet obligation or unverifiable token
the gate never strips or downgrades a disclosure to allow an emit through
exclusions: legal advice or definitive statutory interpretation (escalate to qualified counsel)
right-of-publicity / likeness-and-voice consent screening (delegated to pubrights__likeness_voice)
detection of whether content is synthetic from pixels alone (delegated to a detector); this gate consumes a generation-path classification
operator execution of the allowed emit and downstream content moderation appeals
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for a synthetic-media disclosure and platform-ToS gate, grounded in the EU AI Act, the C2PA/Content Credentials provenance standard, major platform synthetic-media policies, and India's IT Rules and deepfake advisories; no supplied dataset
source_citation: EU Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) Article 50 transparency obligations for AI-generated/manipulated content and deep fakes; C2PA Technical Specification (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) and Content Credentials; Meta, YouTube and TikTok synthetic/manipulated/AI-generated content disclosure policies; India Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules 2021 and MeitY 2023 deepfake advisories

competency_questions.question: How is the emit-action captured and how are the destination platform's ToS constraints resolved?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EMIT_INTAKE normalizes the emit unit and PLATFORM_TOS resolves binding ToS constraints

competency_questions.question: How is the artifact classified as synthetic/manipulated versus authentic, and how is its source-license provenance traced?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SYNTHETIC_MEDIA_CLASSIFY sets the generation path and SCRAPE_LICENSE traces redistribution license

competency_questions.question: What statutory AI-content disclosure obligation attaches to a synthetic artifact, and how does audience context modify it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SYNTHETIC_MEDIA_DISCLOSURE applies EU AI Act Art 50; AUDIENCE_CONTEXT and SYNTHETIC_MEDIA_CLASSIFY set the trigger

competency_questions.question: How are redistribution and reference-only uses distinguished, and how does provenance gate unlicensed source media?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REDISTRIBUTION_VS_REFERENCE and SCRAPE_LICENSE/CONTENT_PROVENANCE gate unlicensed republication

competency_questions.question: How are election-period and minor-audience escalations triggered from audience context?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUDIENCE_CONTEXT feeds ELECTION_INTEGRITY and AGE_PLATFORM_POLICY escalations

competency_questions.question: How do statutory disclosure and platform manipulated-media policy combine for the same artifact?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SYNTHETIC_MEDIA_DISCLOSURE and MANIPULATED_MEDIA_POLICY co-apply, platform possibly stricter

competency_questions.question: How is the full per-jurisdiction and per-platform labeling superset assembled and reconciled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LABELING_REGIMES unions statute and platform rules; MANIPULATED_MEDIA_POLICY and REDISTRIBUTION_VS_REFERENCE feed it

competency_questions.question: How does C2PA provenance carry the disclosure, and how is the manifest made tamper-evident?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTENT_PROVENANCE supplies the manifest; PROVENANCE_SIGNING signs it; IN_BAND_DISCLOSURE_TOKEN carries it

competency_questions.question: How is the applicable jurisdiction set resolved and aggregated into the obligation set?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JURISDICTION_RESOLUTION scopes jurisdictions feeding LABELING_REGIMES and DISCLOSURE_OBLIGATION_SET

competency_questions.question: How are election and minor escalations scoped to the right jurisdictions and audiences?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JURISDICTION_RESOLUTION and AUDIENCE_CONTEXT scope ELECTION_INTEGRITY and AGE_PLATFORM_POLICY

competency_questions.question: How is the disclosure made in-band and non-strippable, and bound to a downstream slot?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IN_BAND_DISCLOSURE_TOKEN, PROVENANCE_SIGNING and DISCLOSURE_SLOT_BINDING make disclosure travel in-band to a confirmed slot

competency_questions.question: How are all obligations aggregated and bound before the handoff?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISCLOSURE_OBLIGATION_SET aggregates obligations and DISCLOSURE_SLOT_BINDING binds them to slots

competency_questions.question: What happens at the fail-closed handoff SPOF when an obligation is unmet or a token may not survive?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FAIL_CLOSED_AT_HANDOFF blocks the emit and HANDOFF_GATE_VERIFICATION verifies token survival

competency_questions.question: How is the gate decision audited and token survival verified at the destination?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HANDOFF_GATE_VERIFICATION re-reads the disclosure and records the decision audit

glossary.definition: image, audio, or video that is artificially generated or substantially manipulated by AI, as opposed to captured-real unaltered media
synthetic or manipulated media that appreciably resembles real persons, objects, places, or events and would falsely appear authentic, the trigger term used in EU AI Act Art 50
a disclosure carried inside the artifact itself (metadata, C2PA assertion, watermark) so it travels with the content rather than as a separable note
the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity standard for a tamper-evident, signed provenance manifest bound to a media asset, surfaced to users as Content Credentials
republishing the actual media bytes to a destination, as distinct from referencing or linking to them
a default that blocks the protected action whenever any required condition is unmet or uncertain, rather than allowing it
the single downstream handoff point at which the disclosure gate is enforced and whose failure determines the whole pipeline's safety
a statutory or platform rule set that mandates a particular synthetic-media disclosure label for a given jurisdiction or platform
media obtained by scraping a platform without a redistribution license, which must not be republished

nodes.definition: Capture and normalize the emit-action as a fixed unit: the concrete artifact about to be published downstream, its generation path (fully synthetic, AI-edited, or captured-real), the destination platform/session, and the asserted publication jurisdiction(s), so every later disclosure and ToS test resolves against one frozen unit of analysis.

base.update_signal: intake schema or emit-action definition changes

pros.claim: A normalized emit unit makes generation-path, platform, and jurisdiction tests resolve against one fixed artifact rather than a moving target
pros.example: 'a fully AI-generated portrait video, posted to TikTok, viewers in the EU' is frozen before any disclosure rule fires

cons.claim: A thin intake (unknown generation path, vague destination) silently weakens every downstream disclosure test
cons.example: an artifact tagged 'maybe edited' with no platform cannot be screened, only escalated

failure_modes: generation path left unknown yet treated as captured-real
destination platform omitted so the wrong ToS set applies
jurisdiction omitted so the wrong labeling regime is applied
acceptance_tests: emit unit records a generation path, a destination platform/session, and at least one asserted jurisdiction
revisit_triggers: intake schema revised
a new generation path (e.g. real-time avatar) appears

nodes.definition: Resolve the destination (and any source) platform's Terms of Service constraints that bind this emit: scraping limits on how source media was obtained, redistribution and republication permissions, API/automation rules, and the platform's own synthetic/manipulated-media policy hooks, so platform-level prohibitions are known before a disclosure plan is built.

base.update_signal: a destination/source platform updates its ToS or developer policy

pros.claim: Reading ToS first means a redistribution prohibition or scraping ban can block an emit before disclosure work is wasted on it
pros.example: TikTok and YouTube ToS forbid redistributing other users' content without permission, independent of any AI label

cons.claim: ToS are unilateral, frequently revised, and per-platform, so a cached snapshot can silently diverge from the live policy
cons.example: a platform tightens its automation policy overnight and a previously allowed bulk emit becomes a violation

failure_modes: stale ToS snapshot applied to a live emit
source-platform scraping limits ignored because only the destination was checked
API rate/automation rule treated as advisory
acceptance_tests: the destination platform's redistribution, scraping, automation, and synthetic-media policy clauses relevant to this emit are identified and dated
revisit_triggers: a platform ToS or developer-policy version changes
a redistribution-permission call is disputed

nodes.definition: Classify the artifact's generation path on the spectrum that triggers disclosure: fully AI-generated, AI-substantially-edited/altered, AI-assisted-but-authentic, or captured-real-unaltered; this classification is the switch that decides whether any synthetic-media disclosure obligation exists at all.

base.update_signal: the AI-content definition or manipulation threshold shifts

pros.claim: An explicit four-way classification makes 'does disclosure apply?' a recorded decision rather than an implicit assumption, matching the EU AI Act's 'artificially generated or manipulated' trigger
pros.example: an AI-generated voiceover is classed fully-synthetic; a colour-graded real clip is captured-real and triggers no AI label

cons.claim: The synthetic/authentic boundary is genuinely fuzzy for AI-assisted edits, and an over-broad threshold floods authentic media with needless labels
cons.example: mild generative denoising of a real photo may or may not cross the 'substantially manipulated' line

failure_modes: substantial AI manipulation mis-classified as authentic, suppressing a required label
trivial AI assistance over-classified as synthetic, mislabeling authentic media
deepfake of a real person not recognized as manipulated media
acceptance_tests: a generation-path class (fully-synthetic, substantially-edited, AI-assisted-authentic, captured-real) is recorded with the evidence that placed it there
revisit_triggers: the AI-content / 'substantially manipulated' definition changes
a borderline AI-edit is mis-classified in review

nodes.definition: Trace how the source media was obtained and whether it carries a redistribution license: SCRAPE-sourced or otherwise unlicensed third-party media must not be republished, so the emit is gated on having either an original/owned source or an explicit redistribution license, independent of any AI label.

base.update_signal: the source-provenance signal or licensing model changes

included: third-party rights in the underlying media

pros.claim: Gating on redistribution license catches unlicensed-republish violations that a synthetic-media label would never surface, since a perfectly labeled AI edit of scraped footage is still an unlicensed republish
pros.example: an AI restyle of a scraped news clip is blocked on the scrape-license gate even though its AI label is correct

cons.claim: Provenance of source media is often unverifiable at emit time, so a conservative gate blocks legitimate fair-use or owned material lacking a paper trail
cons.example: a creator's own footage with no stored license record is treated as unlicensed

failure_modes: scraped/unlicensed source republished under a correct AI label
owned material blocked for lack of a license record
license assumed from platform availability
acceptance_tests: the source is recorded as owned, explicitly licensed for redistribution, or flagged as scraped/unlicensed-and-non-republishable
revisit_triggers: the provenance/licensing model changes
a scraped-source republish is detected post-emit

nodes.definition: Establish the audience context that escalates obligations: estimated reach, whether the content is directed to or likely to reach minors, and the topical sensitivity (political, health, financial), since age and reach determine which heightened platform and statutory rules attach to the same artifact.

base.update_signal: audience-context signals or the minor-directed standard change

pros.claim: Fixing audience context lets the gate apply minor and election escalations to the right emits instead of all of them
pros.example: an AI clip directed to a kids' channel pulls in stricter platform minor rules than the same clip on a general feed

cons.claim: Reach and minor-directedness are predictions, not facts, at emit time, so the context can be wrong in either direction
cons.example: a niche post unexpectedly goes viral into an audience the gate never anticipated

failure_modes: minor-directed content not flagged for heightened policy
reach over-estimated, applying needless escalations
political topical sensitivity missed before an election window
acceptance_tests: an audience context (reach band, minor-likelihood, topical sensitivity) is recorded for the emit
revisit_triggers: the minor-directed standard changes
an emit reaches a materially different audience than predicted

nodes.definition: Apply the mandatory AI-content transparency obligation: under EU AI Act Article 50, deployers of systems that generate or manipulate image, audio, or video constituting deep fakes must disclose that the content is artificially generated or manipulated, in a clear and distinguishable way; this is the central required-label obligation the gate enforces.

base.update_signal: EU AI Act Art 50 transparency scope or guidance changes

pros.claim: Grounding the core obligation in EU AI Act Art 50 gives the gate a concrete statutory anchor: deep-fake content must be disclosed as artificially generated or manipulated
pros.example: Art 50(4) requires deployers to disclose AI-generated or manipulated image/audio/video that is a deep fake

cons.claim: Art 50 carries exceptions (assistive editing, law-enforcement, artistic/satirical works with proportionate disclosure) that a blunt always-label rule mis-handles
cons.example: an evidently artistic synthetic work needs disclosure that does not spoil the work, not a blanket banner

failure_modes: a required deep-fake disclosure omitted entirely
disclosure present but not clear-and-distinguishable
artistic/satirical proportionate-disclosure exception ignored or over-applied
acceptance_tests: a clear-and-distinguishable AI-content disclosure obligation is recorded for any artifact classed synthetic/manipulated, with any applicable exception noted
revisit_triggers: EU AI Act Art 50 transparency guidance changes
a disclosure is found not to be clear-and-distinguishable in review

nodes.definition: Apply destination-platform manipulated-media and synthetic-content policies (Meta, YouTube, TikTok) which independently require labeling or prohibit certain altered/deepfake media; these platform rules co-exist with statute and can be stricter, so the emit must satisfy the platform policy even where statute is silent.

base.update_signal: a platform's synthetic/manipulated-media policy version changes

pros.claim: Honoring platform policy catches removals/penalties statute would not predict, since platforms label and demote unlabeled AI media on their own terms
pros.example: YouTube requires creators to disclose realistic altered or synthetic content; TikTok requires labeling AI-generated content and auto-labels C2PA-marked uploads; Meta labels AI-generated imagery

cons.claim: Platform policies are uneven, fast-changing, and sometimes vaguer than statute, so encoding them risks both over- and under-blocking
cons.example: one platform's 'realistic' threshold differs from another's, and the same artifact is treated differently per destination

failure_modes: destination platform's mandatory AI label not satisfied
a platform-prohibited deepfake category emitted
altered-media policy treated as identical across platforms
acceptance_tests: the destination platform's manipulated/synthetic-media labeling or prohibition rules for this artifact are identified and reconciled with statute
revisit_triggers: a platform synthetic-media policy changes
a platform demotes/removes a correctly-statute-labeled emit

nodes.definition: Use C2PA / Content Credentials as the provenance substrate: a tamper-evident, cryptographically signed manifest bound to the asset that records its creation and edit history (including whether AI tools were used), giving the disclosure a verifiable, machine-readable carrier rather than a strippable visual caption.

base.update_signal: the C2PA spec or Content Credentials adoption profile changes

included: binding of manifest to asset bytes

pros.claim: C2PA gives disclosure a tamper-evident, signed carrier whose alteration is detectable, which a visual caption can never offer
pros.example: a C2PA manifest records that a generative-fill tool edited the image, and any later tampering breaks the signature

cons.claim: C2PA manifests can be stripped by re-encoding or screenshotting, and verification depends on platform support, so provenance is necessary but not self-sufficient
cons.example: a screenshot of a credentialed image drops the manifest, defeating provenance unless a durable in-band mark also exists

failure_modes: provenance manifest absent on a synthetic asset
manifest present but not bound to the asset bytes
provenance relied on where the destination cannot verify it
acceptance_tests: a synthetic/manipulated asset carries a C2PA/Content Credentials manifest binding creation and AI-edit assertions to the asset, with a recorded stripping-risk assessment
revisit_triggers: the C2PA spec or adoption profile changes
a credentialed asset is observed stripped of its manifest

nodes.definition: Assemble the applicable labeling regime set: the union of statutory requirements per asserted jurisdiction (EU AI Act, India IT Rules 2021 and the 2023 deepfake advisories, plus any state synthetic-media laws) and per-destination-platform policy, so the gate reasons over the full superset of labels the emit must carry.

base.update_signal: a jurisdiction adds, amends, or repeals a synthetic-media labeling rule

pros.claim: Treating labels as a superset over all applicable regimes prevents satisfying one jurisdiction while violating another
pros.example: an emit reaching both EU and Indian audiences must satisfy EU AI Act Art 50 and India's IT Rules deepfake-labeling advisories simultaneously

cons.claim: Regimes conflict in form and wording, and stacking every label can produce an over-cluttered or self-contradictory disclosure
cons.example: two regimes mandate differently-worded mandatory captions that cannot both be the single visible label

failure_modes: a jurisdiction's required label omitted from the set
conflicting regime requirements collapsed to the weaker one
platform policy dropped because statute was satisfied
acceptance_tests: the labeling-requirement set is the reconciled superset of every applicable jurisdiction and platform rule for this emit
revisit_triggers: a jurisdiction's labeling law changes
two regimes' label requirements are found to conflict

nodes.definition: Apply heightened election-integrity rules: during defined election periods, synthetic or manipulated political content (especially depicting candidates or officials) is subject to stricter disclosure, prohibition, or removal under platform political-content policies and laws such as India's advisories and EU/state election rules, escalating the obligation for politically-classed emits.

base.update_signal: an election-period rule or window definition changes

pros.claim: Escalating in election windows catches the highest-harm synthetic-media cases where a generic label is insufficient or the content is outright prohibited
pros.example: a synthetic clip of a candidate during an election period can require prominent disclosure or be barred entirely under platform political-deepfake rules

cons.claim: Election periods, jurisdictions, and 'political' scope are hard to define precisely, so the escalation can fire on satire or news or miss novel formats
cons.example: a satirical synthetic skit during an election may be protected expression, not a prohibited deepfake

failure_modes: a prohibited election-period synthetic political emit not blocked
general satire over-blocked as a prohibited deepfake
election window not recognized for the relevant jurisdiction
acceptance_tests: politically-classed synthetic emits in an active election window are escalated to heightened disclosure or block per the applicable rule
revisit_triggers: an election-period rule or window changes
a synthetic political emit is mis-escalated in review

nodes.definition: Apply audience-age and platform minor-protection policies: where content is directed to or likely to reach minors, platform rules and child-safety regimes impose stricter limits on synthetic likenesses, synthetic minors, and advertising, escalating disclosure or prohibition for minor-facing synthetic emits.

base.update_signal: a platform minor policy or child-safety regime changes

pros.claim: Minor-facing escalation blocks the highest-sensitivity synthetic cases (synthetic depictions of or ads to children) that a default label does not address
pros.example: a synthetic depiction of a minor, or AI-personalized advertising to a kids' audience, triggers stricter platform limits than a general AI label

cons.claim: Minor-directedness is a prediction and child-safety regimes vary, so the escalation can over-restrict general content or miss minor reach
cons.example: a general-audience post that incidentally reaches minors may be over-restricted by a minor-directed assumption

failure_modes: synthetic-minor content not blocked under child-safety rules
general content over-restricted as minor-directed
minor reach unaccounted in the escalation
acceptance_tests: minor-directed or minor-likely synthetic emits are escalated to the applicable platform minor and child-safety limits
revisit_triggers: a platform minor policy changes
a minor-facing synthetic emit is mis-handled in review

nodes.definition: Distinguish republishing the media (redistribution, which triggers the full ToS and licensing gate) from merely referencing or linking it (reference-only, which typically does not redistribute the bytes), because the obligation set and the scrape-license gate apply only to actual redistribution, not to a citation or link.

base.update_signal: the redistribution/reference boundary or embedding behavior changes

excluded: statutory AI labeling of original synthetic content

pros.claim: Separating reference from redistribution avoids blocking legitimate citation while still gating actual republication of unlicensed bytes
pros.example: linking to a hosted news clip is reference-only and skips the scrape-license republish gate, whereas re-uploading the clip is redistribution and does not

cons.claim: Embeds and quote-reposts blur the line, since an embed can effectively redistribute the bytes while looking like a reference
cons.example: a platform embed that re-hosts the media is functionally redistribution despite presenting as a link

failure_modes: an embed that re-hosts bytes treated as reference-only
a true reference over-gated as redistribution
quote-repost mis-classified
acceptance_tests: the emit is classified as redistribution or reference-only, and the scrape-license/ToS republish gate is applied only to redistribution
revisit_triggers: the redistribution/reference boundary changes
an embed is found to re-host bytes it was treated as referencing

nodes.definition: Specify the in-band disclosure token: a machine-readable disclosure marker carried inside the artifact itself (embedded metadata, C2PA assertion, and a durable watermark) that the downstream session cannot trivially strip, so the disclosure travels WITH the content rather than as an out-of-band note the next hop can drop.

base.update_signal: the token format or non-strippability requirement changes

pros.claim: An in-band token means a downstream session that re-emits the asset carries the disclosure forward by default, since stripping it requires deliberate tampering rather than mere omission
pros.example: a watermarked + C2PA-marked clip stays disclosed when reposted, whereas a caption-only label is lost on the first re-upload

cons.claim: No single in-band channel is unstrippable: metadata is dropped on re-encode, watermarks degrade, and C2PA breaks on screenshot, so robustness requires redundancy and is never absolute
cons.example: a determined re-encode can defeat any one carrier, so the token must layer several and still cannot guarantee survival

failure_modes: disclosure carried only out-of-band where the next hop can drop it
a single fragile carrier relied on as if unstrippable
token machine-unreadable to the destination
acceptance_tests: the disclosure is carried in-band via at least one durable machine-readable channel, with redundant carriers and a recorded strip-resistance assessment
revisit_triggers: the token format changes
an in-band token is observed stripped at a downstream hop

nodes.definition: Cryptographically sign the C2PA provenance manifest so the disclosure and edit-history assertions are tamper-evident and verifiable by a relying party: any alteration of the asset or its claims after signing breaks verification, turning the disclosure into a checkable claim rather than an editable annotation.

base.update_signal: the signing trust model or certificate policy changes

pros.claim: Signing makes the provenance claim verifiable and tamper-evident, so a relying platform can trust the disclosure or detect that it was altered
pros.example: a C2PA signature lets TikTok verify and auto-apply an AI label from the manifest, and detect if the manifest was edited

cons.claim: Signing depends on key custody and a trust ecosystem; a compromised key, expired cert, or unrecognized trust anchor undermines verification
cons.example: a manifest signed by an untrusted issuer is cryptographically valid but not trusted by the destination

failure_modes: manifest left unsigned, so claims are silently editable
signing key compromise unaddressed
trust anchor not recognized by the destination
acceptance_tests: the provenance manifest is signed by a recognized trust anchor and its tamper-evidence verifies at the destination
revisit_triggers: the signing trust model changes
a signature fails verification at a destination that should trust it

nodes.definition: Bind the required disclosure token to a concrete disclosure slot in the downstream handoff: confirm the destination session/platform exposes a place the in-band token (and any required visible label) can be deposited and will be carried, so the disclosure has a guaranteed home in the next hop rather than an assumed one.

base.update_signal: the downstream handoff contract or available slot changes

pros.claim: Explicitly binding the token to a real downstream slot turns 'the next hop will surely carry it' into a verified property, exposing missing-slot cases before emit
pros.example: confirming TikTok's AI-content toggle and C2PA ingestion exist binds the disclosure to a real slot rather than hoping a caption survives

cons.claim: Downstream slots are heterogeneous and undocumented, and a slot may exist but silently not propagate the token, so binding can give false assurance
cons.example: a platform accepts the metadata field but strips it server-side, so the bound slot does not actually carry the disclosure

failure_modes: disclosure emitted with no bound downstream slot
slot bound but not verified to propagate
visible-label slot assumed but absent
acceptance_tests: each required disclosure is bound to a confirmed downstream slot that is verified to carry it forward
revisit_triggers: the downstream handoff contract changes
a bound slot is found not to propagate the token

nodes.definition: Resolve which jurisdictions' rules actually apply to this emit from the asserted publication geography, audience location, and platform reach, producing the jurisdiction set that LABELING_REGIMES and the escalations reason over, since applying the wrong jurisdiction set silently mis-scopes every obligation.

base.update_signal: the jurisdiction-determination rule or audience-geo signal changes

excluded: the specific statutory text per jurisdiction

pros.claim: Resolving jurisdiction explicitly prevents applying one country's rules to an audience governed by another's, scoping the obligation set correctly
pros.example: an EU-targeted emit pulls in the AI Act, while an India-reaching emit pulls in the IT Rules deepfake advisories

cons.claim: Reach crosses borders and geo-signals are noisy, so the resolved jurisdiction set can be over- or under-inclusive
cons.example: a globally accessible post nominally reaches every jurisdiction, making a literal union impractically broad

failure_modes: a reaching jurisdiction omitted from the set
an inapplicable jurisdiction's rules applied
global reach collapsed to a single home jurisdiction
acceptance_tests: the applicable-jurisdiction set is resolved from publication geography and audience reach and is passed to the labeling and escalation rules
revisit_triggers: the jurisdiction-determination rule changes
an emit is found to reach a jurisdiction not in the resolved set

nodes.definition: Aggregate every triggered obligation into one disclosure-obligation set for the emit: the union of statutory labels, platform policies, provenance/in-band token requirements, redistribution clearances, and any election/minor escalations, with each obligation tagged satisfied or unmet, producing the single checklist the handoff gate enforces.

base.update_signal: any upstream obligation, escalation, or token requirement changes

pros.claim: A single aggregated, per-obligation-tagged set makes the gate's decision a deterministic checklist rather than a scattered set of partial checks
pros.example: the set lists 'EU AI Act label: bound', 'TikTok AI toggle: bound', 'scrape license: missing' so the unmet item is unambiguous

cons.claim: Aggregation hides the provenance of each obligation unless every entry is traceable, and a missing upstream trigger silently shrinks the set
cons.example: if the election escalation never ran, its obligation is simply absent from the set with no signal that it was skipped

failure_modes: an obligation present upstream missing from the aggregated set
obligations aggregated without satisfied/unmet tags
set treated as complete despite a skipped upstream check
acceptance_tests: the obligation set is the union of all triggered obligations, each tagged satisfied or unmet, with traceability to the rule that produced it
revisit_triggers: an upstream obligation or escalation changes
an obligation is found missing from a previously-passed set

nodes.definition: Enforce the fail-closed handoff gate, the single point of failure of the whole pipeline: at the downstream handoff, if any disclosure obligation is unmet, no disclosure slot is bound, or the in-band token cannot be verified to survive transit, the emit is BLOCKED; the gate defaults to block on any uncertainty and never strips or downgrades a disclosure to let the emit through.

base.update_signal: the fail-closed default or block criteria change

excluded: operator execution of an allowed emit

pros.claim: Defaulting to block at the single handoff means a missing or strippable disclosure can never silently leak through; the failure mode is a blocked emit, not an unlabeled synthetic publication
pros.example: an emit whose C2PA slot is unverified is blocked rather than published with a disclosure that the next hop would drop

cons.claim: A strict fail-closed gate at one SPOF over-blocks legitimate emits when an upstream signal is merely uncertain, and concentrates all risk in one component that must itself be highly reliable
cons.example: a transient verification failure on a perfectly compliant emit blocks it, creating pressure to weaken the default

failure_modes: gate fails open and emits without a satisfied obligation
disclosure stripped or downgraded to force a pass
SPOF gate itself unmonitored so its own failure is silent
acceptance_tests: any unmet obligation, unbound slot, or unverifiable in-band token causes the emit to be BLOCKED, with no path that strips or downgrades a disclosure to allow it
revisit_triggers: the fail-closed default or block criteria change
the gate is found to have failed open on any emit

nodes.definition: Verify that the bound in-band token actually survives the handoff and record the gate decision: re-read the disclosure at (or simulating) the downstream destination to confirm the token and visible label are present and verifiable, and write an audit record of the obligation set, the survival check, and the allow-with-disclosure / block outcome.

base.update_signal: the survival-verification method or audit schema changes

pros.claim: Re-reading the disclosure at the destination converts 'the token was attached' into 'the token is present and verifiable where it must be', closing the gap the SPOF most fears
pros.example: a post-emit fetch confirms the C2PA manifest and AI label are intact on the published TikTok asset

cons.claim: True downstream re-read may be impossible before emit, so a simulation can diverge from real platform processing and miss server-side stripping
cons.example: a staging check passes but the live platform's transcoding strips the metadata the staging path preserved

failure_modes: survival assumed rather than verified
audit record omits the obligation set or outcome
simulation diverges from live platform behavior
acceptance_tests: the in-band token's survival is verified (or best-effort simulated) at the destination and an audit record of obligations, survival, and outcome is written
revisit_triggers: the survival-verification method changes
a token verified at emit is found stripped at the live destination

edges.why_related: a failed downstream survival check feeds back to strengthen the in-band token's strip-resistance
verification of token survival validates or invalidates the bound downstream slot
audience location drives which jurisdictions' rules apply
a C2PA manifest lets platforms auto-apply their AI-content label, satisfying platform policy
an unlicensed-scrape redistribution is an unmet obligation that forces a block
signature verification at the destination is the tamper-evidence the survival check relies on
a prohibited election-period synthetic emit is an unmet obligation that forces a block
a minor-protection violation is an unmet obligation that forces a block

edges.resolution_rule: disclosure dominates throughput: when a fail-closed block would stop an emit a publishing SLA wants out, the gate still blocks; throughput is recovered by binding a real disclosure slot, never by stripping or downgrading the disclosure
edges.why_related: the fail-closed disclosure block conflicts with platform/business pressure to publish quickly and frictionlessly
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: satisfy the superset in a single durable carrier: when two regimes mandate differently-worded visible labels that cannot both be the one caption, carry the machine-readable union in-band and render the strictest human-visible label, escalating genuine conflicts to review
edges.why_related: stacking conflicting per-regime label requirements collides with a single in-band token that must carry one coherent disclosure
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: apply the republish gate only to genuine redistribution: classify embeds that re-host bytes as redistribution and subject them to the scrape-license gate, while true reference-only links bypass it
edges.why_related: a permissive reference-only classification can let an embed that actually re-hosts unlicensed bytes escape the scrape-license redistribution gate
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: treat provenance as necessary but not sufficient: a signed C2PA manifest does not by itself satisfy the statutory clear-and-distinguishable disclosure when the destination cannot verify it, so require a human-perceptible label in addition where provenance may be stripped
edges.why_related: relying on C2PA provenance to discharge the statutory disclosure conflicts with provenance being strippable and unverifiable at some destinations
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

conflict_axes.name: disclosure_mandatory_vs_publishing_throughput
conflict_axes.description: Fail-closed disclosure blocks maximize transparency but add friction and can stop emits a publishing pipeline wants out fast.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: recover throughput by binding a real disclosure slot, never by weakening the disclosure

conflict_axes.name: in_band_robustness_vs_strippability
conflict_axes.description: In-band tokens travel with the content but no single carrier is unstrippable, so robustness needs redundancy and is never absolute.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: layer metadata, C2PA, and watermark; verify survival; default to block on doubt

conflict_axes.name: statutory_label_vs_platform_policy
conflict_axes.description: Statute and platform policy can both apply and diverge in form and strictness for the same artifact.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: take the reconciled superset and satisfy the strictest applicable rule

conflict_axes.name: over_labeling_vs_under_labeling
conflict_axes.description: A broad synthetic threshold floods authentic media with needless labels; a narrow one suppresses required disclosures.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: calibrate the substantial-manipulation threshold and escalate borderline cases to review

conflict_axes.name: redistribution_gate_vs_legitimate_reference
conflict_axes.description: Gating republication protects rights but can over-block legitimate citation and fair reference.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate only genuine redistribution; treat byte-re-hosting embeds as redistribution

conflict_axes.name: jurisdiction_union_vs_practical_scope
conflict_axes.description: Global reach makes a literal union of all jurisdictions' rules impractically broad, while a narrow home-jurisdiction scope under-covers.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: resolve jurisdictions from actual audience reach, not nominal global availability

conflict_axes.name: election_escalation_vs_protected_expression
conflict_axes.description: Heightened election rules catch high-harm political deepfakes but can over-block satire and news.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: escalate candidate-depicting deceptive synthesis; preserve clearly-marked satire and news per exception

conflict_axes.name: minor_protection_vs_general_audience_reach
conflict_axes.description: Minor-directed escalations protect children but can over-restrict general content that incidentally reaches minors.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: escalate on directed-to-minors signals; treat incidental reach proportionately

conflict_axes.name: single_spof_gate_vs_distributed_enforcement
conflict_axes.description: Concentrating enforcement at one fail-closed handoff is simple and auditable but makes that gate a single point of failure that must be highly reliable.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the SPOF gate but monitor it heavily and verify token survival downstream

edge_cases.description: The downstream destination exposes no disclosure slot, so an in-band token cannot be deposited or carried.
edge_cases.trigger: DISCLOSURE_SLOT_BINDING finds no slot that propagates the token at the handoff
edge_cases.mitigation: fail closed and BLOCK the emit; do not publish a disclosure the next hop will drop

edge_cases.description: A correctly C2PA-marked synthetic asset is screenshotted or re-encoded downstream, stripping the manifest and the disclosure.
edge_cases.trigger: the in-band token's only durable carrier is defeated by re-encode/screenshot
edge_cases.mitigation: layer redundant carriers (watermark + metadata + C2PA) and verify survival; block if none survive

edge_cases.description: A deepfake of a real person is mis-classified as authentic, suppressing the required AI-content disclosure.
edge_cases.mitigation: calibrate the manipulation threshold conservatively and escalate borderline cases to review

edge_cases.description: An AI restyle of scraped, unlicensed source footage is emitted with a correct AI label but is still an unlicensed republish.
edge_cases.trigger: SCRAPE_LICENSE gate skipped because the AI disclosure looked sufficient
edge_cases.mitigation: run the scrape-license redistribution gate independently of the AI label and block unlicensed republication

edge_cases.description: Two applicable jurisdictions mandate differently-worded mandatory visible labels that cannot both be the single caption.
edge_cases.trigger: LABELING_REGIMES superset contains conflicting human-visible label requirements
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the machine-readable union in-band, render the strictest visible label, and escalate true conflicts to review

edge_cases.description: A synthetic clip depicting a candidate is emitted during an active election window without the heightened election disclosure or block.
edge_cases.trigger: ELECTION_INTEGRITY escalation not triggered for the resolved jurisdiction
edge_cases.mitigation: detect election windows per jurisdiction and escalate candidate-depicting synthesis to prominent disclosure or block

edge_cases.description: An embed that re-hosts the underlying media bytes is treated as reference-only and escapes the redistribution gate.
edge_cases.mitigation: classify byte-re-hosting embeds as redistribution and subject them to the scrape-license gate

edge_cases.description: The fail-closed handoff gate itself fails open on a transient verification error, publishing an unlabeled synthetic emit.
edge_cases.trigger: the SPOF gate defaults to allow instead of block on an internal error
edge_cases.mitigation: default to block on any internal/verification uncertainty and monitor the gate's own health

edge_cases.description: A provenance manifest is signed by an issuer the destination platform does not trust, so the disclosure is valid but not honored.
edge_cases.trigger: PROVENANCE_SIGNING uses an unrecognized trust anchor
edge_cases.mitigation: sign with a trust anchor the destination recognizes and add a human-perceptible label as fallback

edge_cases.description: A general-audience synthetic post unexpectedly reaches a minor audience that the gate never escalated for.
edge_cases.mitigation: apply proportionate minor protections on minor-likely reach and re-evaluate on reach signals

edge_cases.description: A cached platform ToS snapshot diverges from the live policy, so a now-prohibited redistribution is allowed.
edge_cases.mitigation: date ToS snapshots, refresh on a schedule, and treat staleness beyond a bound as an unmet obligation

edge_cases.description: An obligation triggered upstream is silently absent from the aggregated set because its producing check was skipped.
edge_cases.trigger: DISCLOSURE_OBLIGATION_SET aggregates without verifying every upstream check ran
edge_cases.mitigation: require each upstream check to register a present/absent status; a skipped check is itself an unmet obligation

workflow.description: Normalize the emit-action into a fixed unit: artifact, generation path, destination platform/session, and asserted jurisdictions.
workflow.gate: generation path, destination, and >=1 jurisdiction recorded

workflow.description: Resolve destination and source platform ToS: scraping, redistribution, automation, and synthetic-media clauses, dated.
workflow.gate: relevant ToS clauses identified and dated

workflow.description: Classify the artifact as fully-synthetic, substantially-edited, AI-assisted-authentic, or captured-real.
workflow.gate: a generation-path class is recorded with evidence

workflow.description: Trace source provenance and redistribution license; flag scraped/unlicensed source media.
workflow.gate: source recorded as owned, licensed, or scraped/non-republishable

workflow.description: Apply EU AI Act Art 50 deep-fake disclosure with any artistic/assistive exception noted.
workflow.gate: clear-and-distinguishable disclosure obligation recorded for synthetic artifacts

workflow.description: Assemble the per-jurisdiction and per-platform labeling superset and reconcile conflicts.
workflow.gate: reconciled superset of statute and platform labels assembled

workflow.description: Build the in-band token via C2PA assertion, metadata, and durable watermark; sign the manifest.
workflow.gate: disclosure carried in-band via >=1 durable signed channel

workflow.description: Resolve the applicable jurisdiction set from publication geography and audience reach.
workflow.gate: applicable jurisdiction set resolved from actual reach

workflow.description: Apply election-period and minor-audience escalations to politically- or minor-classed emits.
workflow.gate: election and minor escalations applied per resolved jurisdiction and audience

workflow.description: Bind each required disclosure to a confirmed downstream slot verified to carry it.
workflow.gate: each required disclosure bound to a propagating downstream slot

workflow.description: Aggregate all triggered obligations into one set, each tagged satisfied or unmet, with traceability.
workflow.gate: every triggered obligation present and tagged satisfied/unmet

workflow.description: Block on any unmet obligation, unbound slot, or unverifiable token; then verify survival and write the audit.
workflow.gate: emit allowed-with-disclosure only if all obligations met and token survival verified; else blocked

dominance_rules.rule: FAIL_CLOSED_AT_HANDOFF must BLOCK the emit whenever any obligation in DISCLOSURE_OBLIGATION_SET is unmet, no slot is bound, or token survival is unverifiable
dominance_rules.rationale: the handoff is the SPOF; failing open publishes an unlabeled or strippable synthetic emit
dominance_rules.trigger: an emit reaches the handoff with an unmet obligation or unbound slot
dominance_rules.action: block the emit and route to remediation; never strip or downgrade the disclosure

dominance_rules.rule: A disclosure may never be stripped or downgraded to make an emit pass the gate
dominance_rules.rationale: stripping defeats the entire purpose of mandatory in-band disclosure
dominance_rules.trigger: a pass would require removing or weakening a required disclosure
dominance_rules.action: block instead and escalate for a compliant disclosure slot

dominance_rules.rule: SYNTHETIC_MEDIA_DISCLOSURE statutory obligation dominates platform-policy convenience but never overrides a stricter platform rule
dominance_rules.rationale: both regimes co-apply; the strictest applicable rule governs
dominance_rules.trigger: statute and platform policy diverge for the same artifact
dominance_rules.action: satisfy the reconciled strictest superset from LABELING_REGIMES

dominance_rules.rule: SCRAPE_LICENSE redistribution gate must run independently of any AI-content disclosure
dominance_rules.rationale: a correct AI label does not license republication of scraped source media
dominance_rules.trigger: an emit redistributes third-party media with only an AI label
dominance_rules.action: block on missing redistribution license regardless of the AI label

dominance_rules.rule: IN_BAND_DISCLOSURE_TOKEN must use redundant durable carriers and survival must be verified before allow
dominance_rules.rationale: no single carrier is unstrippable; an out-of-band note can be dropped by the next hop
dominance_rules.trigger: disclosure carried only out-of-band or via a single fragile carrier
dominance_rules.action: require layered in-band carriers and a survival check

dominance_rules.rule: ELECTION_INTEGRITY and AGE_PLATFORM_POLICY escalations dominate the default label for in-scope emits
dominance_rules.rationale: election and minor contexts carry the highest harm and stricter or prohibitive rules
dominance_rules.trigger: a politically- or minor-classed synthetic emit in an in-scope window or audience
dominance_rules.action: apply the heightened disclosure or block before the default label

dominance_rules.rule: JURISDICTION_RESOLUTION must be fixed before LABELING_REGIMES finalizes the obligation superset
dominance_rules.rationale: the wrong jurisdiction set silently mis-scopes every label
dominance_rules.trigger: labeling assembled before jurisdictions are resolved from reach
dominance_rules.action: resolve jurisdictions from actual audience reach first

dominance_rules.rule: DISCLOSURE_OBLIGATION_SET must record every upstream check as present or absent
dominance_rules.rationale: a silently skipped check shrinks the set and hides an unmet obligation
dominance_rules.trigger: an obligation is absent because its producing check did not run
dominance_rules.action: treat a skipped upstream check as itself an unmet obligation

dominance_rules.rule: PROVENANCE_SIGNING alone does not discharge the statutory clear-and-distinguishable disclosure where the destination cannot verify it
dominance_rules.rationale: provenance is necessary but strippable and not always verifiable downstream
dominance_rules.trigger: a signed manifest relied on at a destination that cannot verify it
dominance_rules.action: add a human-perceptible label in addition to provenance

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not build the in-band token before the labeling superset is reconciled; a late regime adds a label the token must re-carry
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-signing and re-binding the token after a missed jurisdiction's label surfaces

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize the obligation set before jurisdiction resolution; a late jurisdiction invalidates the whole set
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-aggregating every obligation after the jurisdiction scope changes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not bind a downstream slot without verifying it propagates the token; an unverified slot silently drops the disclosure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-emitting after discovering the bound slot stripped the disclosure server-side

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not rely on a single in-band carrier; retrofitting redundancy after a strip incident requires re-marking every asset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: emergency re-watermarking of already-published assets after a stripping incident

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not run the AI-disclosure path while skipping the scrape-license gate; an unlicensed republish surfaces as a takedown later
anti_rework_rules.prevents: post-publication takedown and re-clearance of unlicensed redistributed media

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not classify embeds as reference-only without checking byte-re-hosting; mis-classification leaks an ungated redistribution
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-screening embeds after an ungated republish is discovered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not let the SPOF gate default to allow on internal errors; a single fail-open publishes an unlabeled emit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: incident response and recall after an unlabeled synthetic emit leaks through a fail-open gate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not cache platform ToS indefinitely; a stale snapshot permits a now-prohibited redistribution
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-clearing emits after a ToS change invalidates a cached redistribution permission

iteration_protocol.trigger: an in-band token is observed stripped at a downstream hop
iteration_protocol.action: strengthen redundant carriers in IN_BAND_DISCLOSURE_TOKEN and re-verify survival in HANDOFF_GATE_VERIFICATION

iteration_protocol.trigger: the fail-closed gate is found to have failed open on any emit
iteration_protocol.action: force default-to-block on uncertainty in FAIL_CLOSED_AT_HANDOFF and add health monitoring of the SPOF gate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a deepfake is mis-classified as authentic, suppressing a required label
iteration_protocol.action: recalibrate the manipulation threshold in SYNTHETIC_MEDIA_CLASSIFY and escalate borderline cases

iteration_protocol.trigger: an unlicensed scraped source is republished under a correct AI label
iteration_protocol.action: enforce the independent redistribution gate in SCRAPE_LICENSE and REDISTRIBUTION_VS_REFERENCE

iteration_protocol.trigger: a prohibited election-period synthetic political emit passes the gate
iteration_protocol.action: tighten election-window detection in ELECTION_INTEGRITY scoped by JURISDICTION_RESOLUTION

iteration_protocol.trigger: a reaching jurisdiction's required label is missing from the obligation set
iteration_protocol.action: re-run JURISDICTION_RESOLUTION from actual reach and re-assemble LABELING_REGIMES

iteration_protocol.trigger: a minor audience is reached without the minor escalation
iteration_protocol.action: tighten minor-likelihood signals in AUDIENCE_CONTEXT and apply AGE_PLATFORM_POLICY proportionately

iteration_protocol.trigger: a stale platform ToS permits a now-prohibited redistribution
iteration_protocol.action: refresh and date the snapshot in PLATFORM_TOS and treat staleness as an unmet obligation

priority_rationale: EMIT_INTAKE/PLATFORM_TOS/SYNTHETIC_MEDIA_CLASSIFY are foundational; the regime and provenance nodes build the obligation superset; the in-band token and slot binding make disclosure survive; FAIL_CLOSED_AT_HANDOFF is the SPOF that blocks on any gap and HANDOFF_GATE_VERIFICATION closes the loop.
